answers.explanation: Accounting and resource allocation serve the shared system, not a single user's work.
In shared memory the processes touch the same memory; in message passing the OS carries the data.
All three are sources of errors the OS has to notice and handle.
Accounting, used for billing or usage statistics.
Protection controls all access to resources; security adds authentication and defense from outsiders.
The shell just looks the name up and runs whatever program it finds.
That's its whole job, repeated forever.
macOS: Aqua on top, UNIX underneath.
A separate program would only change its own directory.
Commands in a file, run unattended: batch.
